summary: Tests-only diffs skip every gate signal: lib/review-depth.ts:63 (classifyDiff, the `codeLike` guard). Gate tags from the gate scan, a gate scan that could not run (null), GATE_PATH matches and deletions are only checked when the class is already code. A diff that touches only test paths therefore stays in the "tests" class even when the gate scan tags an RH hunk (a skipped test, a relaxed threshold) or the scan failed. The tests class gets only the testing specialist: no <reader>, no native adversarial pass and no <reader> (planReview, line 191 onward). This happens in this repo today. E2E_KINDS and CASE_QUARANTINE live in test/helpers/touchfiles-data.ts and test/helpers/periodic-exclude-data.ts, and both classify as tests. So a PR that changes trial counts or quarantines a case gets the lightest review. Deleting test files is also invisible, because deletedCode filters to the code class. The class table in docs/review-policy.md says a tagged hunk makes the diff "gate", and the "skipped test" trigger can only fire from a test file, so as written that trigger can never fire. Fix: apply `gateTagged > 0`, `gateTagged === null` and GATE_PATH whenever the class is tests or higher; add the eval-policy helper paths to GATE_PATH; count deleted test files as a gate signal.

summary: A quiet revise skips re-review based on the cited decisions, not on the plan change: lib/autoplan-revise.ts:171-174. `quiet` only checks that every `--incorporates` id resolves below High, that no phase was added and that docs-only still holds. It never looks at the plan delta. An unattended driver can cite one Medium decision and rewrite any part of the Implementation plan. The snapshot is then rebound to the new hash (ps.snapshot = newHash) without review. Because `capped = quiet ? [] : ...`, a phase that has already used its round cap also loses the cap_delta owner gate item. So the unreviewed delta reaches neither a reviewer nor the owner, and the only trace is a journal row. Fix: compute lineDiff on the quiet path too and require a small delta. Whenever a touched phase is at its cap, still record cap_delta and regate, so quiet never suppresses the owner item.

label: High
summary: **An unrelated plan rewrite can inherit completed reviews.** `lib/autoplan-revise.ts:169–188` decides that the entire revision needs no review solely from the severities of the IDs supplied to `--incorporates`. It never establishes that the actual delta only implements those decisions. With one pending Medium amendment, an author can also remove an idempotency requirement or change authentication behavior, without adding a phase. `quiet` remains true, every closed phase's snapshot is rebound to the unreviewed hash, and an amendment run can become complete. Require a reviewed delta or equivalent independent confirmation before rebinding; the severity of the original finding does not bound the risk of its implementation.

label: High
summary: **A detected test-gate relaxation skips adversarial coverage.** `lib/review-depth.ts:63–68` only considers gate signals after the paths already classify as code. A test-only change that skips a security regression or relaxes an assertion remains `tests` even when the gate scanner positively tags it. A read-only reproduction with `paths:["test/security.test.ts"], gateTagged:1` returned only the testing specialist: no <reader> or <reader>. `gateTagged:null` produces the same result. Promote positive gate findings independently of the initial path class, and handle unavailable test-gate coverage conservatively.

label: High
summary: **Carry can certify a different commit with the checkout's pregate.** `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:369–375,493–500` verifies the pregate against the current working tree but labels it current for the separately supplied `--head`. Nothing requires that argument to equal the checkout's HEAD. From a clean checkout at reviewed commit A, `carry --head B --pregate <A's result>` can carry to an eligible descendant B containing changed tests or a base merge, while reporting A's checks as current for B. The PR-head comparison also accepts B when B is pushed. Require the selected head to equal the checked-out head, or verify against B's actual tree before publishing.

label: Medium
summary: **Fix-check evidence bypasses the existing snapshot binding.** `ship/sections/<reader>.md.tmpl:236–242` starts a `review` token but finishes a `review-fix-check` row. That skill is absent from `DIFF_REVIEWS` in `lib/review-evidence.ts:8`, so `bindReview` returns before consuming the token or comparing start/end content, and `reviewFreshness` ignores the row. A direct call reproduced a supposedly clean fix-check with no `review_binding` and no freshness result. Changes during the check therefore go undetected, and the previous full review remains stale rather than being safely superseded. Add explicit fix-check binding and compatible start-token ownership without treating a narrow check as a full pass.

label: Medium
summary: **Fixture capture force-deletes a shared branch it does not own.** `scripts/review-dispatch-compare.ts:115–128` force-resets the fixed branch `gsta131-capture-base`, then unconditionally deletes it in `finally`, even if worktree creation failed. Git branches are shared across worktrees: an existing branch loses its ref, and concurrent captures can replace or delete each other's comparison base, corrupting the resulting measurements. Pass the parent commit directly as the base, or use a unique, ownership-tracked ref and remove only that ref.

The default gate-scan path is never run by a test. Every CLI test passes --gate-tagged 0, so nothing checks the GATE_SUMMARY tagged={RH-1:2,...} parse, the fail-closed null when gstack-gate-diff exits non-zero or changes its format, or a non-numeric --gate-tagged becoming null. If the regex drifts, every code diff silently becomes gate class, or a tagged hunk is read as 0.

summary: The quiet path rebinds every touched phase to the new plan hash without re-review whenever the cited decisions are below High. Nothing limits the edit to those decisions, so one Medium id can carry any Implementation-plan change past review. It also clears capped, so a post-cap delta no longer becomes an owner gate item. decisionSeverity's reduce also lets a known severity outrank an unrecognized one (['high','Medium'] resolves to Medium).
fix: Use the quiet path only when the delta is bounded (for example lineDiff size, or touched sections that match the decisions), keep the capped owner gate item, and return 'unknown' for any severity not in SEVERITY_ORDER.

summary: The fix-check path cannot pass Step 11.5. Step 9.4 applies fixes (item 2) before it logs the pass (items 4 and 6), so a pass that fixed anything has review_binding start_wtree != end_wtree (state 'changed'). Step 11.5 requires both to equal the adversarial record's wtree. The old loop always reached Step 11 through a later full pass with no edits. Under the new table, the common case (pass 1 fixes only below-floor items, then one fix-check, then NEXT: done) leaves that 'changed' pass as the final skill:'review' record, because the fix-check logs as review-fix-check. So 11.5 blocks and reinserts a fresh full Step 9: a pass the plan says not to run, or a loop. Also, decision 3.5 takes a '--start review' token for a 'review-fix-check' row, but bindReview returns early for skills outside DIFF_REVIEWS. The token is never consumed and the fix-check row carries no content binding.
fix: Define what Step 11.5 binds after a fix-check: for example, the fix-check row as the final record with its own start capture under a DIFF_REVIEWS skill, plus a start/end comparison on the fixed tree. Or have 11.5 accept the pass record plus a fix-check whose start wtree equals the pass's end wtree. Add review-fix-check to captureReviewStart and bindReview.

summary: Gate signals are evaluated only when the class is already code. The gate scan's RH rules fire mainly in test files: RH-1 for removed test declarations and skip idioms (some only at test floor), RH-3 for snapshots, and RH-15 for relaxed thresholds. So a diff that only skips or deletes tests, or loosens a threshold, stays tests class and gets core plus the testing specialist, with no <reader>, adversarial pass or <reader>. docs/review-policy.md says a tagged hunk makes the diff gate class. TEST_PATH also classes test/helpers/** (for example carve-guards.ts, eval harness and selection code) and fixtures as tests, so edits to guard code there skip escalation the same way.
fix: Apply the gateTagged > 0 check (and the null fail-closed check) to tests class too, and add a unit case: classifyDiff({paths:['test/a.test.ts'], gateTagged:1}).class === 'gate'.

label: FIXABLE
summary: 1. [CRITICAL] [FIXABLE] Step 11's adversarial pass and <reader> are silently skipped on every ship where pass 1 applies any fix. Files: ship/sections/<reader>.md(.tmpl) "Review plan", ship/sections/adversarial.md(.tmpl) header, lib/review-depth.ts planReview (the history.fullPasses === 0 branch). The ship control flow runs Steps 1-21 in order, and a Step 9 repeat goes in "before the pending Step 10". So Step 11 only runs after the Step 9 loop has converged. The prose tells the parent to keep the latest plan ("a repeat uses decision 2's run. Save its REVIEW_PLAN: line"). That run has --pass >= 1, so planReview prints "SKIP: <reader> and <reader> (run once, on pass 1)". On the fix-check route, the plan holds only the fix-check dispatch. The new Step 11 header says to run the native pass "only on DISPATCH: <reader> ... otherwise print ADVERSARIAL: skipped (review plan)". The result is that the adversarial and cross-family voices never run on a PR whose first pass fixed even a nit, and that is the common case. The "always-on / Every diff gets the Claude adversarial pass" text right below the header now contradicts it, so model behaviour becomes nondeterministic. Under diff-plus-blocking and all, there is no decision-2 run at all, so which plan applies is undefined. Fix: base "run once" on whether Step 11 has actually run (an adversarial-review row exists, or a --step11-done flag), not on fullPasses. Alternatively, have Step 11 read pass 1's saved plan explicitly. Then rewrite the always-on sentence so it agrees.

summary: 2. [CRITICAL] [FIXABLE] A tests-class diff ignores every gate signal. File: lib/review-depth.ts classifyDiff (the codeLike guard). Gate-scan tags (relaxed threshold, skipped test), a failed or absent gate scan (gateTagged === null) and GATE_PATH hits are only checked when the class is already code or higher. The repo's gate policy lives under test/: test/helpers/test-selection.ts holds CASE_QUARANTINE and E2E_KINDS, and paths like test/*pregate*.test.ts exist. So a diff that quarantines a case, changes a case kind, adds a skip or loosens a threshold, all inside test/, classifies as "tests". That class dispatches only the testing specialist: no <reader>, no adversarial pass, no <reader>. This contradicts docs/review-policy.md, which says a tagged hunk makes the diff gate class, and AGENTS.md's gate-integrity rules. Fix: apply gateTagged > 0 and GATE_PATH whatever the class, and treat a null scan as gate (at least code) for the tests class as well.

label: FIXABLE
summary: 3. [CRITICAL] [FIXABLE] A non-stamp package.json edit can pass as "stamp-only" and get zero reviewers. File: bin/gstack-review-plan (the stampOnly filter). The check is line-based: /^[+-]\s*"version"\s*:/ anchors only the start of the line. A changed line that starts with "version" and carries more keys on the same line (for example an added lifecycle script; JSON allows that layout) matches. If that is the whole diff, every package.json in it is stamp-only, so the class is docs: core checklist only, with no specialists, no adversarial pass and no <reader> (NOT_CLAIM strips the version string, so the numbers trigger does not fire). Install-time code then lands with the shallowest review. Fix: JSON.parse both blobs, delete .version from each and deep-compare. Treat any parse failure as not stamp-only.

summary: 4. [HIGH] [FIXABLE] Any git failure in gstack-review-plan fails open to the docs class. File: bin/gstack-review-plan (git() returns null, and every caller coerces it with ?? ''). If git diff --name-status times out (60 s limit), hits ENOBUFS or errors, paths is empty, so the class is docs with "no changed paths" and nothing is dispatched. A numstat failure sets diffLines to 0, so the <reader> never fires on code. If the -U0 diff passes 64 MB (big goldens or lockfiles), the numbers scan comes back empty and the <reader> is dropped for docs and tests diffs. The policy states "errors fail closed", but this path fails open. Fix: when any required git call returns null, exit nonzero or force the gate class.

summary: 5. [HIGH] [FIXABLE] The gate scan's unread hunks count as clean. File: bin/gstack-review-plan (the GATE_SUMMARY parse). Only tagged={...} is summed. GATE_SUMMARY also reports unread=N: hunks the scan could not inspect. A run with unread > 0 and nothing tagged yields gateTagged = 0, so the diff stays code class and the gate escalation is lost exactly where the scan was blind. Fix: if unread > 0, set gateTagged = null (fail closed to gate).

summary: 6. [HIGH] [INVESTIGATE] A "quiet" revise lets an arbitrary plan rewrite through without review. File: lib/autoplan-revise.ts (the quiet predicate and the rebound loop). The check covers only the severities of the --incorporates decisions (below High), that no phase was added, that docs_only still holds and that the touched phases are closed. Nothing bounds or inspects the edit itself. Incorporating one Medium decision while also rewriting unrelated parts of the Implementation plan rebinds every touched phase's snapshot to the new hash, prints APPLIED, and approval follows. The capped-delta path records a diffStat and raises an owner gate item; the quiet path does neither. In an unattended run, the agent writing the edit is the same one choosing --incorporates. Fix (human judgment needed): limit the delta, for example by size or by the plan_items the decisions name. Otherwise surface it as a gate item the way cap_delta is.

summary: 7. [MEDIUM] [FIXABLE] The CRITICAL-triggered <reader> and the user's force flags are not wired into the ship flow. Files: lib/review-depth.ts planReview, ship/sections/<reader>.md decision 2. criticalFound is only known after the specialists return, but the pass-1 plan is computed before dispatch, and decision 2's command passes neither --critical-found, --force nor --gated. summary: 8. [MEDIUM] [FIXABLE] Autoplan's docs-only detection misreads agent-read prose as docs. File: lib/autoplan-scope.ts docsClassPath. The skill-directory test only checks the top-level directory. capy/skill/gstack/*.md has top = "capy", and capy/SKILL.md does not exist, so it counts as docs although capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md exists. summary: 10. [MEDIUM] [INVESTIGATE] carry --pregate can certify a head that was never checked. File: bin/gstack-ship-receipt cmdCarry and pregateFieldFor. verifyPregate checks the checkout's working tree, but the field is labelled "current for <head>", and head can come from --head. Nothing compares --head with rev-parse HEAD; the dirty-tree check does not. In gh mode the pushed head must equal --head, but the checkout can be any clean commit. So a pregate for the checkout gets published as current for the PR's pushed head. Fix: refuse --pregate unless head equals the checkout's HEAD.

summary: 1. **High — Tagged test bypasses never receive gate-class review.** `lib/review-depth.ts:63–69` only examines `gateTagged`, auth scope and gate paths inside `if (codeLike)`. A test-only change therefore remains `tests` even when the gate scanner positively identifies a disabled security test or relaxed assertion. I reproduced a change from `test(...)` to `test.skip(...)` in `test/auth.test.ts`: `scanCandidate` returned `tagged:{"RH-1":1}`, but `planReview` with that tag and `SCOPE_AUTH=true` dispatched only the testing specialist and explicitly skipped the <reader>, native adversarial reviewer and <reader>. An author can weaken the gate precisely where the new policy promises mandatory adversarial coverage. Apply positive gate signals independently of the initial path class; ordinary untagged tests can retain the cheaper path.

label: High
summary: 2. **High — A below-High decision can approve an unrelated, unreviewed plan rewrite.** `lib/autoplan-revise.ts:170–188` determines `quiet` solely from the severity of the IDs supplied through `--incorporates`, closed phases and whether another phase enters scope. It never establishes that the revision contains only those decisions' changes. Given a pending Medium disagreement, a caller can incorporate that ID while replacing the backend implementation with an unrelated design, including removing authentication or changing data-retention behavior, provided it stays within the existing phases. Every phase's snapshot is then rebound to the new hash without a review, and the amendment-completion path can mark the run complete. Before this change, the changed implementation hash reopened the reviews or produced a capped-delta owner gate. Preserve that gate for unverified extra changes rather than treating an existing Medium decision as authorization for the entire replacement plan.

label: Medium
summary: 3. **Medium — A successful fix-check cannot replace the stale review evidence left by fixes.** `ship/sections/<reader>.md.tmpl:236–242` starts a `review` token but logs the result as `review-fix-check`, then exits the review loop. That skill is absent from `DIFF_REVIEWS` in `lib/review-evidence.ts:8`, so `bindReview` returns before consuming or validating the token and creates no `review_binding`; `reviewFreshness` returns no verdict for it. The latest actual `review` row remains changed/nonconverged after the fixes, and the dashboard only selects `review` or `plan-eng-review` for Eng Review. A direct reproduction returned no freshness for a clean fix-check and `STALE` for the preceding changed review. Thus the newly supported normal below-floor-fix path cannot persist fresh, cleared review evidence, and also leaves its start token unconsumed. Bind fix-check evidence explicitly and teach the readiness consumer how it completes the preceding reviewed baseline without counting it as another full pass.

label: Medium
summary: 4. **Medium — Fixture capture overwrites and deletes a shared local branch.** `scripts/review-dispatch-compare.ts:115–128` force-moves the fixed branch name `gsta131-capture-base`, then unconditionally deletes it in `finally`. Git branches are shared across linked worktrees, so an existing branch with that name loses its original tip, potentially leaving unpushed work unreachable. Even an invalid `--capture` SHA reaches the deletion before this invocation created any branch. Concurrent captures also overwrite/delete each other's base and can record a fixture against the wrong commit. Pass the parent commit SHA directly as the base, or allocate a unique owned ref and delete it only after successful creation.
